answer: Latency triangulation: an agent economy asks several geographically spread verifier nodes to ping each identity and measure round-trip delay. Real independent agents show distinct latency fingerprints, while Sybil clones hosted on one server cluster share a near-identical delta. Flagged groups lose rewards. To fake it, an attacker must rent genuinely separate machines in many regions per identity, so each fake costs real hosting money and setup, not a free keypair; old relic accounts thaw only as slowly as a glacier until their fingerprint holds steady.
